title: Hollis AI - time to first token & hosting options discussion

transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-09-08
Time: 11:00 AM CDT
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Jin Park (Redwood SE), Maya Thompson (CTO, Hollis AI), Liam O'Connor (ML Engineer), Priya Rao (Security), Benji (UX)

Auto-summary (auto): quick discovery, fairly high interest in fast onramp, security constraints, wants numbers and pilot plan

[00:00] Samir: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. I'm Samir from Redwood, AE on the account. quick intro round?
[00:12] Maya: Hi, Maya Thompson, CTO at Hollis. we build document understanding for insurance, we want to add a generation/assistant layer.
[00:24] Liam: Liam, ML eng. Looking at latency constraints, budget.
[00:28] Priya: Priya, security. i'll be asking about data retention and key management.
[00:33] Jin: Jin Park, SE, I'll handle the technical fit and benchmarks.

[01:05] Samir: Cool. high level — you're looking to evaluate Redwood's hosted API first as a PLG/self-serve quickstart and then decide whether dedicated or private makes sense. is that fair?
[01:18] Maya: yeah, we want to get to first token quickly; product team wants a demo in 2 weeks and infra needs the security answers before a pilot.
[01:27] Liam: our latency SLO is 150ms 95th for short chat prompts, and cost per 1k tokens matters for the POC economics.

[02:00] Jin: quick note: our hosted API supports streaming, function/tool calling, and has model variants you can pin. if you need private, we support VPC mode and a private control plane; both options are used in production.

[02:28] Maya: how long to get running with hosted — like from signup to first token? we have a small dev team, want minimal friction.
[02:36] Samir: typical time-to-first-token (ttft) is under an hour for a simple test — sign up, API key, try playground or curl. for a production prototype we usually see teams get to meaningful demos in 2–5 days with the free credits we provide.
[02:53] Benji: do you mean free credits? how many, like what can we run?
[03:00] Samir: we'll propose a credits package tailored to your expected usage; for example a 2-week pilot for a team of 5 we'll usually offer X compute credits (we'll include an exact calc).

[03:35] Priya: from security perspective, we need SOC 2 type II, KMS/HSM integration, SSO/SAML, and audit logs. do you have sample artifacts?
[03:46] Jin: yes — we have SOC2 summary and a security pack. we can do customer-managed keys via KMS and we keep detailed audit logs token-level. for VPC there's private networking and optional on-prem bundle for air-gapped customers.
[04:10] Priya: and data retention? we can't have PII leave our account for some workloads.
[04:17] Jin: hosted has options — by default request data is processed to provide the service but we have contracts and a privacy mode for no-retention for inputs; for strict cases we'd usually recommend dedicated/reserved or private deployment so you control retention fully.

[04:55] Liam: ok, can you explain dedicated vs private in terms of throughput and cost? like if we start with hosted and then grow.
[05:05] Samir: Dedicated is reserved GPU pools for your workloads — predictable throughput and lower per-token cost at scale; private (VPC or on-prem) is for stricter security/isolation and sometimes lower latency since it's colocated with your infra. Hosted gives fastest time-to-value.
[05:25] Maya: how about fallbacks? if dedicated capacity is saturated, will we be routed to hosted?
[05:33] Jin: yes, policies allow routing by latency/cost/region. we also support automatic fallback to a compatible model variant. fallback rules are configurable per-project.

[06:12] Benji: on latency — you mentioned streaming. our UX needs sub-200ms p99 for short responses, is that possible without expensive hardware?
[06:23] Jin: it depends on model and prompt length. small conversational models at optimized kernels can hit that on good infra. we can recommend batching and KV-cache strategies but batching trades latency for throughput; our platform offers continuous batching tuned per SLO.

[07:05] Maya: What about quantization? we have budget constraints and want to test 4-bit or 8-bit quantized models to cut cost.
[07:15] Jin: we do quantization-friendly execution paths; we can show model+quantization recommendations after we understand your token distribution. quantized models lower cost but there may be a small quality delta.

[07:50] Liam: For benchmarking, what's the best way to validate TTFT and p95/p99? do you have a runbook?
[07:58] Jin: yes — we'll share a short TTFT benchmark runbook: sample payloads, concurrency patterns, and scripts to run against hosted endpoints. ideally run with your real prompt set so quality/regression is visible.

[08:40] Maya: also, our legal team will want pricing examples and a path to reserved capacity if we scale.
[08:48] Samir: we'll include a pricing calc showing sample monthly cost at 100k, 1M tokens and a reserved commit option.

[09:10] Priya: on SSO — does Redwood support SAML and role-based access? we need RBAC for teams and audit trails for compliance.
[09:19] Jin: yes SSO via SAML/OIDC and RBAC with token-level audit trails. we'll attach docs.

[10:05] (background murmur)
[10:20] Liam: if we run the hosted pilot, can we see Cold start timings and model warmups? we care about real-world p95 during spikes.
[10:30] Jin: the runbook includes warmup patterns and cache priming. for consistent p95 we recommend a small warm pool or dedicated on-demand nodes. Cold starts are mostly model-size dependent.

[11:05] Maya: Could you do a quick example of flow — dev picks a model, pins version, we call API — how does rollout work?
[11:13] Samir: Sure: you deploy to a route, you can pin a model version, create a canary rollout to 10% traffic, run automatic quality checks on eval sets; if regression detected we can auto-fallback to previous model.
[11:36] Benji: that auto-fallback is handy.

[12:00] (short pause)
[12:12] Priya: One more compliance Q — where are logs stored regionally? we need EU residency for some customers.
[12:20] Jin: regioning is supported. you can choose region for data residency, and private deployments can of course be entirely in your VPC/region.

[12:48] Liam: competitors — have you seen issues switching from Anthropic/OpenAI? curious about migration and prompt parity.
[12:56] Samir: we onboarded customers who migrated — differences often require prompt tuning; we can help with example prompts and evaluation harnesses.

[13:30] Maya: ok, talk about SLOs and SLAs — for enterprise we care about uptime and latency SLOs.
[13:40] Samir: Dedicated and Private come with SLA-backed uptime and latency targets. Hosted has strong guarantees for self-serve customers too — we'll include our SLA summary.

[14:05] Jin: for the pilot, SE will provide a minimal benchmark plan: a short load test, latency profile, and quality checks on the prompt set.

[15:00] Benji: what about observability? product wants token-level cost breakdown per route.
[15:08] Samir: Redwood Console provides token-level cost, per-model dashboards, tracing hooks, and error analysis. we can share screenshots and a short video.

[15:40] Maya: any gotchas in VPC peering? our infra team is sensitive about network egress.
[15:48] Jin: VPC peering requires a few small firewall rules and a TLS endpoint. we provide a network diagram and a checklist. for air-gapped on-prem, we have a packaged deploy but that takes longer.

[16:20] Liam: timeline — if we accept the pilot, when can we start?
[16:27] Samir: assuming paperwork, we can start the hosted pilot within 48 hours; for VPC it's usually 1–2 weeks to configure; on-prem takes longer (several weeks).

[17:10] (crosstalk)
[17:18] Priya: if we need customer-managed keys, is HSM supported?
[17:25] Jin: yes, KMS/HSM integrations supported — we'll attach the KMS integration notes.

[18:00] Maya: Great. what do you need from us to start the pilot?
[18:06] Samir: a small prompt sample set, expected concurrency/volume, and the list of stakeholders. then we'll provision credits and a test route.

[18:38] Benji: How will billing look during credits? do we get invoices?
[18:45] Samir: credits offset usage; we'll provide a simple billing projection and an invoice option if needed.

[19:20] (short pause)
[19:30] Jin: i'll also note that for performance-sensitive paths we can recommend kernel/memory settings; sometimes model choice + sequence length optimization is the low-hanging fruit.

[20:12] Maya: ok, i'm comfortable moving forward with a hosted pilot to validate TTFT and UX. after that we'll decide if dedicated or VPC is required.

[20:30] Samir: awesome; we'll send the credits/pricing calc and the TTFT runbook. propose pilot window w/c 2026-09-20?
[20:40] Maya: that works for us, i'll confirm with infra.

[21:05] (wrap-up)
[21:12] Samir: recap: Redwood to send pricing/credits calc, SOC2/security pack, KMS notes, TTFT runbook; schedule SE deep dive next week with infra; Hollis to confirm pilot stakeholders and date.
[21:30] Maya: yep, thanks everyone. looking forward.
[21:36] Jin: thanks all, i'll follow up with the runbook and a short benchmark script.
